He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks basketball|Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks]]. ==Early life== Harris was born and grew up in [[Ellenwood, Georgia]] and attended [[Martin Luther King Jr. High School (Lithonia, Georgia)|Martin Luther King Jr. High School]]. As a senior, he averaged 15.8 points and 11.8 rebounds per game and led the team to a 24–6 record and the Class 5A state semifinal.{{cite web|title=Kevon Harris ready to be next big name in the NBA|url=https://www.kltv.com/2019/05/01/kevon-harris-ready-be-next-big-name-nba/|website=KLTV.com|date=April 30, 2019|access-date=March 10, 2020}} After high school, Harris completed a [[postgraduate year]] at [[DME Academy]] in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]].{{cite web|title=Kevon Harris Recruiting (2016)|url=https://www.prephoops.com/2016/04/kevon-harris-recruiting-2016/|work=PrepHoops|date=25 April 2016|access-date=March 10, 2020}} He signed with [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks basketball|Stephen F. Austin]] for college basketball over offers from [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]], Texas A&M and [[UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|UT-Arlington]]. ==College career== Harris became a starter for the Lumberjacks during his true freshman season, averaging 8.5 points and 3.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Game Notes:2017–18 Men's Basketball|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/sfajacks.com/documents/2018/2/2/MBBNotesatLU2318.pdf|work=Stephen F. Austin Athletics|access-date=March 10, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} As a sophomore, he averaged 14.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists per game and was named second team All-[[Southland Conference]].{{cite web|title=Southland Conference Preseason Awards: Marlain Veal, Stephen F. Austin clean up the hardware|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2018/10/5/17935280/southland-conference-preseason-awards-marlain-veal-stephen-f-austin-season-review-2019|website=MidMajorMadness.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 5, 2018|access-date=March 10, 2020}} Harris averaged 17.8 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.0 steals as a junior and was again named second team All-Southland Conference. He surpassed the 1,000 point milestone during the season. He initially declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], but opted to return to Stephen F. Austin for his senior season. Harris became the school's all-time leading scorer at the Division I level on February 19, during a 14-point performance in a win over [[Central Arkansas Bears men's basketball|Central Arkansas]], passing [[Thomas Walkup]].{{cite web|first1=Caleb|last1=Beames|first2=Stephanie|last2=Frazier|title=SFA's Kevon Harris sets school's DI scoring record|url=https://www.kltv.com/2020/02/20/sfas-kevon-harris-sets-schools-di-scoring-record/|website=KLTV.com|date=February 19, 2020|access-date=March 10, 2020}} Following the end of the regular season, Harris was named the [[Southland Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and first team All-Southland Conference.{{cite web|title=Harris, Kensmil, Keller receive top Southland honors|url=https://www.ktre.com/2020/03/09/harris-kensmil-keller-receive-top-southland-honors/|website=KRTE.com|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 10, 2020}} He finished fourth in the conference in scoring with 17.5 points per game and also averaged 5.7 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Burgess|title=Southland Basketball: 2020 conference tournament preview and predictions|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/03/10/southland-basketball-2020-conference-tournament-preview-predictions/2/|website=BustingBrackets.com|publisher=FanSided|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 19, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Raptors 905 (2020–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Harris was selected 11th overall in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|January 2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|first=Soheil|last=Jamshidi|title=Raptors 905 Select Kevon Harris and Gary Payton II in the 2021 NBA G League Draft.|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-select-kevon-harris-and-gary-payton-ii-in-the-2021-nba-g-league-draft|website=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=January 11, 2021}} On August 20, 2021, Harris signed with [[KK Zadar|Zadar]] of the [[HT Premijer liga]] and the [[ABA League]].{{cite web|title=Former 'Jack Kevon Harris heading overseas to join top Croatian team|url=https://www.kltv.com/2021/08/20/former-jack-kevon-harris-heading-overseas-join-top-croatian-team/|website=KLTV.com|date=August 20, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}} On October 6, 2021, he parted ways with Zadar.{{cite web|title=Kevon Harris napušta KK Zadar; "Zbog obiteljskih problema bio je dekoncentriran, pokušali smo mu pomoći na razne načine"|url=https://www.antenazadar.hr/clanak/2021/10/kevon-harris-napusta-kk-zadar-zbog-obiteljskih-problema-bio-je-dekoncentriran-pokusali-smo-mu-pomoci-na-razne-nacine/|website=antenazadar.hr|date=October 7, 2021|access-date=October 6, 2021|language=Croatian|trans-title=Kevon Harris leaving Zadar; "Because of family problems, he was not focused, we tried to help him in many ways"}} Harris rejoined the Raptors 905 in October 2021.{{cite news|first=Blake|last=Murphy|title=Raptors 905: 10 storylines to follow for 2021–22 G League season|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-905-10-storylines-follow-2021-22-g-league-season/|website=Sportsnet.ca|date=November 5, 2021|access-date=November 14, 2021}} ===Orlando Magic (2022–2024)=== Harris joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612750/timberwolves|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 26, 2022}} In his Summer League debut, Harris scored thirteen points in a 85–77 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets vs Minnesota Timberwolves Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/den-vs-min-1522200008/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 26, 2022}} On July 25, 2022, Harris signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] on a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Kevon Harris to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-kevon-harris-nba-two-way-contract-release-story-20220725|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 25, 2022}} On December 29, he was suspended by the NBA for one game without pay due to coming off the bench during an altercation in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]] the day before.{{cite web|title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions|website=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2022|access-date=December 31, 2022}} ===College Park Skyhawks (2024–2025)=== On September 18, 2024, Harris signed an [[Exhibit 10]] deal with the [[Atlanta Hawks]],{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Hawks Sign Kevon Harris To Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/hawks-to-sign-kevon-harris-to-exhibit-10-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 18, 2024|access-date=September 20, 2024}} but was waived on October 18.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Hawks Waive Kevon Harris, Daeqon Plowden|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/hawks-waive-kevon-harris-daeqon-plowden.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}} On October 26, he joined the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Finalize Training Camp Schedule and Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/college-park-skyhawks-finalize-training-camp-schedule-and-roster/n-6159937|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} On March 1, 2025, Harris signed a 10-day contract with the Hawks.{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Kevon Harris to a 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-kevon-harris-to-a-10-day-contract|access-date=April 3, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} He did not appear in a game before his contract was terminated on March 4, when Atlanta signed [[Dominick Barlow]] to a standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Kevon Harris: Contract terminated|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kevon-harris-contract-terminated/|access-date=April 3, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2025)=== On July 3, 2025, Harris signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |last2=read |first2=Rockets Wire·2 min |date=2025-07-03 |title=Rockets signing former Magic wing Kevon Harris to two-way contract |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/rockets-signing-former-magic-wing-213921187.html |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} He was waived by Houston on December 2 following the signing of [[Tyler Smith (basketball, born 2004)|Tyler Smith]], having played for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], but never appearing in a game for the parent club Rockets.{{Cite web|title=Rockets Add Tyler Smith, Part with Kevon Harris|url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/onsi/news/rockets-add-tyler-smith-part-with-kevon-harris|access-date=December 6, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} === Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2025–present)
